fixes.explanation: That's what He says. “I will gather all the nations and bring them down to the Valley of Jehoshaphat.” (Joel 3:2) He says it for the time when He restores Judah and Jerusalem. All the nations are included, friend.
Close, but scattering is something the nations did. The LORD says Israel is the one “…whom they have scattered among the nations…” (Joel 3:2) What He does with the nations is gather them.

Good guess, but the text never brings up trade routes. The LORD says the judgment is “…concerning My people, My inheritance, Israel…” (Joel 3:2) After that He lists what was done to His people and His land, and He says they took His silver and gold. (Joel 3:5)

Babylon is a famous name, but it's not in this passage. The LORD says they sold the people of Judah and Jerusalem “…to the Greeks, to send them far from their homeland.” (Joel 3:6) The verse names the Greeks as the ones they were sold to.

That's what He says. “I will sell your sons and daughters into the hands of the people of Judah…” (Joel 3:8) Then the people of Judah will sell them to the Sabeans, a distant nation. The same thing they did to Judah comes back around to them, which is what He meant by returning it on their heads.

Sit down, that's the one. “…for there I will sit down to judge all the nations on every side.” (Joel 3:12) The nations are told to be roused and advance to the Valley of Jehoshaphat. He is the one who sits down to judge them.

Near is the word. “For the Day of the LORD is near in the valley of decision.” (Joel 3:14) Not far off, not already past. Just before that, the verse says, “Multitudes, multitudes in the valley of decision!”
Not over, friend. The verse says, “For the Day of the LORD is near in the valley of decision.” (Joel 3:14) It speaks of multitudes in the valley, and it says the Day is near, not over.
True. “The sun and moon will grow dark, and the stars will no longer shine.” (Joel 3:15) Even the lights in the sky go dim. That comes right after the verse that says the Day of the LORD is near.
It's true, friend. Joel 3:15 says, “The sun and moon will grow dark, and the stars will no longer shine.” The prophecy says that about the sky, so True is the right answer.

That's it. “But the LORD will be a refuge for His people, a stronghold for the people of Israel.” (Joel 3:16) The verse says the LORD will roar from Zion and raise His voice from Jerusalem, and heaven and earth will tremble. Even then, He is a refuge and a stronghold for His people. That's a comfort.

Not that one, friend. The text says, “The LORD will roar from Zion and raise His voice from Jerusalem…” Then it says, “But the LORD will be a refuge for His people, a stronghold for the people of Israel.” (Joel 3:16) That's what He is for them.
Not that one, friend. The verse says, “The LORD will roar from Zion and raise His voice from Jerusalem…” (Joel 3:16) He raises His voice, and for His people He is “a refuge” and “a stronghold.”
False, you got it. “Jerusalem will be holy, never again to be overrun by foreigners.” (Joel 3:17) The words are “never again,” so foreigners will not overrun it. That's the promise, friend.

Right, from the house of the LORD. “…a spring will flow from the house of the LORD to water the Valley of Acacias.” (Joel 3:18) The spring flows from His house to water that valley. The verse also says all the streams of Judah will run with water.

Briefly would be a short stay, and that's not what the text says. “But Judah will be inhabited forever, and Jerusalem from generation to generation.” (Joel 3:20) Egypt and Edom are the ones left desolate. Forever is a whole lot longer than a quick visit.
